text:
Jeremy Swayman kept Boston in this game far longer than it had any right to be. Carolina outplayed the Bruins from the second period on, and Sebastian Aho's backhand at 10:19 of the third finally turned that pressure into a 2-1 win at Lenovo Center. Aho, drafted 35th overall in 2015 out of Kärpät, had five shots on goal and a goal on a 15 percent chance.

The play bore out how lopsided it was. Carolina had 64 shot attempts to Boston's 39 and 4.1 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) to the Bruins' 1.86. Our simulation of every shot gives the Hurricanes an 84 percent chance of winning a replay. The second period was the clearest stretch: Carolina out-chanced Boston 1.95 to 0.14 in expected goals. Swayman saved 2.1 goals more than his 30 shots against deserved, while Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 14 of 15 for a 0.86 edge. Carolina went 0 for 4 on the power play despite 1.17 expected goals, so the margin could have been wider.

Boston got on the board first, Pavel Zacha scoring on a first-period power play 1:31 in, with Elias Lindholm and David Pastrnak assisting. Jackson Blake tied it with 52 seconds left in the period, a wrist shot off a Nikolaj Ehlers pass. Blake, picked 109th overall in 2021 and a North Dakota product, was named first star and also missed a 47 percent look in the third that went off target. The facts we have don't include standings or streaks for either club, so the result is simply a deserved win for Carolina and a game Boston stole for 50 minutes.
